questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the passage gives the controlling distinction: at 80 bpm one minute gives 80 pulses. On that basis "eighty pulses" is the supported choice. Option A ("one hundred sixty pulses") fails because it doubles the tempo; Option B ("sixty pulses") fails because it uses 60 bpm instead of 80; Option C ("one hundred pulses") fails because it uses 100 bpm instead of 80.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The beat and the measure in simple meter

stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about the beat and the measure in simple meter. 5/4 has five quarter-note beats per measure. A marginal reminder adds: top number gives beats in simple meter. A reader must decide which of the four proposed statements the note warrants, without using outside knowledge.

questions.stem: Working from “Count beats in 5/4 / Top number gives beats in simple meter. / The beat and the measure in simple meter”, which answer is consistent with the note?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: 5/4 has five quarter-note beats per measure. On that basis "five quarter-note beats" is the supported choice. Option A ("four beats") fails because it confuses with 4/4; Option C ("three beats") fails because it confuses with 3/4; Option D ("ten beats") fails because it counts eighth notes.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The beat unit in compound metre

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: Each 6/8 bar has two dotted-quarter beats, so three bars have six. A marginal reminder adds: two beats per 6/8 bar. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: For this question the reminder is “Count beats in 6/8 three bars / Two beats per 6/8 bar. / The beat unit in compound metre”. Which answer matches the evidence?

answer.exemplar: Three bars of 6/8 compound duple meter contain six dotted-quarter beats total, two per bar.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: each 6/8 bar has two dotted-quarter beats, so three bars have six. On that basis "Three bars of 6/8 compound duple meter contain six dotted-quarter beats total, two per bar" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The total duration of a measure

stimulus.body: A short reference note on the total duration of a measure is set for a close-reading task. It states: At 100 bpm one beat lasts 0.6 seconds, and 5/4 has five beats, so one measure lasts three seconds. A marginal reminder adds: multiply 0.6 by five. Four statements are then offered, and only one of them follows from what the note actually says.

questions.stem: The check to perform is “Compute 5/4 measure at 100 bpm / Multiply 0.6 by five. / The total duration of a measure”. Which option passes that check?
questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: at 100 bpm one beat lasts 0.6 seconds, and 5/4 has five beats, so one measure lasts three seconds. On that basis "The total duration of a measure" is the supported choice.
